cards.q: What is the member's preservation age?
aliases: what age can i access my super
when can i access my super

sources.label: Table: "Your date of birth" against "Preservation age"

ato.quote: Your preservation age depends on when you were born, as shown in this table.
Your preservation age is not the same as your pension age.

cards.detail: Anyone under 60 today was born after 1 July 1964, so their preservation age is 60: retiring before 60 doesn't release their super.

cards.q: What are the conditions of release?
aliases: when can i get my super
how do i get my super
cards.a: Retiring permanently at or after preservation age; leaving a job on or after 60; turning 65; permanent incapacity; a balance under $200 when leaving a contributing employer; death.
cards.detail: Early access in limited cases: compassionate grounds (ATO), severe financial hardship, terminal medical condition. Retiring counts only at or after preservation age, which is 60 for everyone under 60 today.

sources.quote: ceasing an arrangement of employment on or after the age of 60,
having an account balance of less than $200 when you terminate employment with an employer who contributed to UniSuper

ato.quote: You turn 65 years old, even if you're still working.
You reach your preservation age and choose to retire.

cards.q: What do preserved, restricted and unrestricted non-preserved mean?
cards.a: Preserved: needs a condition of release (most contributions and all earnings). Restricted non-preserved: usually released on leaving a contributing employer. Unrestricted non-preserved: available any time.

sources.quote: Member and employer contributions made into super and all investment earnings must be preserved.
Unrestricted non-preserved benefits can generally be accessed at any time

cards.q: Can a member get super early for financial hardship?
cards.a: Possibly, if receiving eligible Commonwealth income support. They apply to UniSuper (the Trustee). Call 1800 331 685 to go through options.

sources.quote: You must be receiving eligible government income support benefits to qualify.

ato.quote: When you can access super early due to severe financial hardship and how to apply.

cards.q: How does early release on compassionate grounds work?
cards.a: The member applies to the ATO directly, not UniSuper.

sources.quote: you must apply directly to the ATO

ato.quote: Eligibility criteria, required evidence and what to do before applying to access super on compassionate grounds.

cards.q: How does access for a terminal medical condition work?
cards.a: Two registered medical practitioners (one a specialist) certify less than 24 months to live. Apply to the Trustee. DBD inbuilt benefits use 12 months. Early access may end insurance or inbuilt benefits.

sources.quote: if you get certification that you have less than 24 months to live from two registered medical practitioners
the inbuilt terminal medical condition benefits is 12 months

ato.quote: How to access your super early if you have a terminal medical condition.

cards.q: Is a lump sum withdrawal taxed?
cards.a: From 60, generally tax-free. Under 60, drawn proportionally from taxable and tax-free components; below preservation age the taxable component is taxed at 22% or the marginal rate, whichever is lower.

sources.quote: If you're age 60 or over, the lump sum benefit paid to you will generally be tax-free.
tax will be withheld from the entire taxable component at a rate of 22% or your marginal tax rate, whichever is lower

cards.q: What tax is withheld from a benefit with no TFN?
cards.a: Under 60 with no TFN: 47% of the taxable component.

sources.quote: If you're under 60 and haven't provided your TFN, we're required to withhold 47% tax of the taxable component of benefits paid to you.

cards.q: How do temporary residents claim super when leaving Australia?
cards.a: Through a Departing Australia Superannuation Payment once the visa has expired or been cancelled and they've left. Taxed 35% (65% for working holiday makers). Unclaimed after six months it goes to the ATO, with no exit statement.

sources.quote: is generally subject to withholding tax of 35% (or 65% for working holiday makers)
If temporary residents don't claim their super within six months of departing Australia, we'll transfer it to the ATO and we won't provide an exit statement.

ato.quote: How to deal with superannuation if you are a temporary visa holder.

cards.q: What happens to super when an Australian moves overseas?
cards.a: It stays with UniSuper until a condition of release is met. Moving permanently to New Zealand, it can go to a KiwiSaver account tax-free.

sources.quote: Even if you're living and working in another country, your super can stay with UniSuper.
Transfers to a New Zealand KiwiSaver Scheme aren't taxed.

cards.q: Does a retired member have to withdraw their super?
cards.a: No. It can generally stay in UniSuper.

sources.quote: Even if you've stopped making contributions and have retired, you don't have to withdraw your super
